name: IBM 5155
summary: IBM’s transportable desktop-class PC, packaged around an integrated display and full-height expansion architecture.
focus: Document the chassis, installed adapters, storage configuration, display condition, and any surviving software or transport accessories.

name: Osborne 1
summary: An early mass-market portable computer built around CP/M, dual floppy drives, and a compact integrated display.
focus: Preserve boot media, application disks, drive alignment notes, keyboard condition, and the machine’s distinctive portable enclosure.

name: Panasonic Senior Partner
summary: A distinctive all-in-one portable PC compatible from Panasonic, combining the system, display, and peripherals into one transportable package.
focus: Record the installed options, internal cabling, display and drive behavior, integrated peripherals, and any Panasonic-specific documentation.

name: Compaq Portable II
summary: A second-generation Compaq portable that carried desktop PC compatibility into a more refined transportable system.
focus: Inventory expansion cards, storage, memory, display condition, BIOS behavior, and any Compaq diagnostics or setup media.

name: Tandy 1000 TL
summary: A member of Tandy’s 1000 family, known for its approachable home-computing design and enhanced graphics and sound compatibility.
focus: Catalog the motherboard revision, memory, storage, audio and video behavior, keyboard, software bundle, and expansion hardware.

name: Commodore VIC-20
summary: Commodore’s approachable early home computer, centered on cartridge software, cassette or disk storage, and direct television output.
focus: Preserve power-supply details, video output, keyboard and cartridge condition, peripheral compatibility, and software media.

name: Commodore 64
summary: The original breadbin-style Commodore 64: a widely used home computer with a deep library of software, peripherals, and music hardware.
focus: Record board revision, SID and VIC variants, power supply, video quality, keyboard, serial peripherals, cartridges, and disk images.

name: Commodore 64C
summary: A redesigned Commodore 64 in the later low-profile enclosure, retaining the platform while changing its industrial design and internal revisions.
focus: Document case and keyboard condition, board revision, custom chips, power supply, video output, peripherals, and preserved software.

name: Commodore 128
summary: Commodore’s expanded 8-bit system, combining native C128 operation with Commodore 64 compatibility and a CP/M mode.
focus: Test each operating mode, document video outputs, inspect memory and custom chips, and preserve compatible disks and peripherals.

name: Amiga 500
summary: The keyboard-integrated Amiga that brought the platform’s graphics, audio, and multitasking environment into a broadly accessible home system.
focus: Catalog motherboard and chipset revisions, Kickstart, memory expansions, floppy behavior, video output, peripherals, and disk images.

name: Amiga 1000
summary: The original Amiga model and the machine that began this preservation journey in 2011.
focus: Preserve Kickstart and Workbench media, document motherboard and expansion details, test video and audio, and record the system’s provenance.

name: Epson Apex 100
summary: A compact Epson desktop PC compatible representing the practical, work-focused DOS systems that populated homes and offices.
focus: Inventory CPU, memory, storage, display adapter, expansion cards, keyboard, Epson utilities, and surviving software media.
